param_count_measured.note: measured via DecoderLM.num_parameters() in hindi/model/model.py, checkpoint 2 self-check. Slightly below docs-phase-2/depth_width_tradeoff.md's 24.4M estimate: that estimate's +0.1M pos-embed term assumed learned absolute positions, but the actual choice (RoPE) has zero learned position parameters.

schedule.notes: picked via smoke_test.py's LR sweep on real data (mps) at batch_size=32; candidates [0.0001, 0.0003, 0.0006, 0.001] over 50 steps each, min_lr = peak_lr / 10 (standard nanoGPT convention). See viva-lma.md for the sweep results.

results.note: rejected: only 1.6% faster than batch_size=32 while 6.5% worse on fixed-token-budget loss, exceeding the 5% quality tolerance (max acceptable was 6.2662)

not measured: candidate hit an apparently-unbounded Apple MPS Graph JIT shader-compilation stall for this batch shape on this hardware (confirmed via process sampling: stuck in MPSGraph encodeToCommandBuffer / commitAndContinue creating a new command buffer, not a hang or bug in the sweep code). Killed after 12+ minutes with zero step progress on a 50-step throughput probe. Hardware/backend characteristic, not something to fix in code.

batch_size_sweep.notes: picked via smoke_test.py's batch-size sweep on real data (mps). batch_size=64 was measured and rejected (worse loss-per-token than the 5% tolerance allows despite negligible speedup); batch_size=128 could not be measured in practical time due to a one-time MPS shader-compile stall. batch_size=32 (the original default) wins on the actual evidence, not because larger batches weren't tried. See viva-lma.md 2026-08-29 entries for full reasoning and the process-level diagnosis.
